question: Should gil_free=True become from_pymc's default?

arm_definitions.default: owalnuts.from_pymc(model) (PyTensor C backend, Python callable), threads=1
arm_definitions.numba: owalnuts.from_pymc(model, mode='NUMBA') (the same numba-compiled function gil_free wraps, as a Python callable), threads=1: the bit-identity control
arm_definitions.gilfree: owalnuts.from_pymc(model, gil_free=True) (numba cfunc, C ABI), threads 1 and 4

robustness.note: 50 separate child processes per model, each a full 4 x 1,000/1,000 gil_free run at threads=4 on the same seed; a fault is a nonzero exit, a timeout, or a status other than ok; a non-identical result is a draw hash differing from rep 1

functionals: every unconstrained coordinate (+ theta_1..8 for eight)
order: breadth: seeds outer, models in list order, the 4 arms rotated by (seed index + model index); then robustness: models outer, reps 1..50

metrics.bit_identity: sha256 of the (chains, draws, dim) retained draws; gilfree t1 vs numba t1 (same compiled function), gilfree t1 vs t4, gilfree t1 vs default
metrics.wall_ratio: median over seeds of gilfree wall per gradient / default wall per gradient, both threads=1 (Rust-side wall / target calls); also gilfree t4 / default t1
metrics.agreement: per seed: max over functionals of |mean_gilfree - mean_default| / sqrt(mcse_gilfree^2 + mcse_default^2)
metrics.gates: cells passing R-hat <= 1.01, bulk/tail ESS >= 400, zero retained divergences

predictions.P1: gilfree t1 is bit-identical to numba t1 on every model and seed where both run (same compiled function)
predictions.P2: gilfree is bit-identical at threads 1 and 4 on every model and seed
predictions.P3: gilfree is NOT bit-identical to the default C backend on most models (identical on at most 3 of 10 runnable models): C and numba compile different elementwise code (WP47: equal on gauss100 only; WP78: unequal on eight and hier). The brief's expectation was 'identical'; this preregistration disagrees and records both
predictions.P4: gilfree t1 / default t1 wall per gradient in [0.1, 0.9] on every runnable model
predictions.P5: agreement: max |z| <= 5 on every seed of every model where both arms pass the gates
predictions.P6: gates: gilfree passes at least as many cells as default on every model
predictions.P7: errors: initvals_data fails under gilfree with NotImplementedError at construction (the documented PyMC >= 5.28 snapshot limitation) while the default runs; no other model errors under any arm
predictions.P8: robustness: 0 faults and 0 non-identical results in 150 runs

propose_default_iff: R1: 0 models where gilfree errors (construction, sampling, fault or timeout) where the default succeeds, other than the known initval + pm.Data limitation, and that limitation fails closed with NotImplementedError before sampling and is documented with a fallback (from_pymc(model) at threads=1, or the gil_free=False switch)

R2: 0 models where gilfree differs where the default succeeds; 'differs' = (a) gilfree not bit-identical to numba on any seed, or (b) gilfree passes fewer gate cells than default, or (c) agreement max |z| > 5 on >= 2 of 3 seeds
R3: robustness 0 faults and 0 non-identical results
decision_rule.note: Bit identity with the C-backend default is reported but is not a rule clause: a default change from C to numba changes the draws for a given seed by construction, which the CHANGELOG would state. The rule decides a proposal only; no default is changed in this study. API compatibility (gilfree returns a CFuncTarget, not a callable; refresh= needs the callable transport) is recorded per cell and reported as a separate requirement for any default change.
